detail.longDescription: How can I ensure style rules for extended component take precedence over style rules for the component I am extending using vanilla extract? Assuming code like this: // my-component.css.ts import { style } from "@vanilla-extract/css"; export const root = style({ background: "green", fontWeight: "bold", }); export const awesome = style({ background: "red", }); // MyAwesomeComponent.tsx import * as styles from "my-component.css.ts"; const MyAwesomeComponent = ({ className, ...props }) => ( <div className={[styles.root, className].join(" ")} {...props} /> ); // MyMoreAwesomeComponent.tsx const MyMoreAwesomeComponent = ({ className, ...props }) => ( <MyAwesomeComponent className={[styles.awesome, className].join(" ")} {...props} /> ); I find that MyMoreAwesomeComponent gets two classes added to it, both of which have a style rule for background. Both have the same specificity, so it's up to source order of the compiled app to determine which background to use. How can I make sure MyMoreAwesomeComponent overrides the background with its own value. I need a general pattern to use, not just for this one instance.
